quick.topic: Decide what the prototype must prove
quick.summary: Why three weeks of prototyping answered nothing, and the question to write first.
quick.takeaway: One question per prototype. Build only what answers it.

parts.title: Decide what the prototype must prove

beats.line: I spent three weeks on a full prototype. After testing, we still could not decide. Why?
What question was it built to answer?
Whether the new booking flow is good, I suppose.
Good is too wide to test. Pick one thing it must prove.
For example: can people change a booking without help?

board.text: can they change a booking alone?

beats.line: Then build only the screens that answer it.
Doesn’t a fuller prototype teach us more?
It teaches a little about everything, and nothing for certain.
Question: can they change a booking alone? Four screens, ready by Thursday.
And on Friday you will have an answer.

quiz.question: What should you decide before building a prototype?
options: The one question it must answer
How many screens the product has
Which tool to build it in
quiz.explanation: The question decides which screens to build and at what detail, and makes the test result usable.

quiz.question: A prototype that covers every screen always gives clearer answers than a focused one.
quiz.explanation: A focused prototype built around one question gives a clear answer faster.
